feedback: Written before this candidate has raced, so it states no outcome for it. Your wheel_track narrowing is the only geometry change that has raised the score: 0.12 to 0.09 m (iteration 3) took the score from 55.1 to 57.9, and 0.09 to 0.08 m (iteration 4) took it to 58.5. Iteration 2 showed that a forward sensor lead at y=0.07 and a lighter body (0.6 kg, shorter) both cut s-bend progress from 0.163 to 0.119, so keep y=0.05 and mass 0.8 kg. Body width has no effect on the off-track limit, since max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4) stays at 0.06 m. For wheel_radius 0.04 m, I scaled kp to 1.0 and kd and ki by 0.75 to keep yaw gain near iteration 4, so the race reads speed rather than extra turn gain. When the race reports: if progress rises above 0.2 and steering_oscillation stays at or below about 0.2, keep wheel_radius 0.04 m. If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with max_error still at 0.06 m, the speed gain is causing overshoot, so raise mass before adding gain.
requested_changes: If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.2 with max_error still at the 0.06 m floor: raise mass from 0.8 kg to 0.9 kg, with the other geometry held. Evidence: iteration 2's lighter body (0.6 kg) cut s-bend progress from 0.163 to 0.119, so added inertia is the safer damping lever.

If progress rises above 0.2 with steering_oscillation at or below about 0.2: keep wheel_track 0.08 m and wheel_radius 0.04 m, and test wheel_radius 0.045 m next. Evidence: iterations 3 and 4 showed narrowing the track raised progress on the s-bend (0.163 to 0.178 to 0.185), so turn and speed gains are working together.

Do not return wheel_track to 0.12 m or move the sensors to y=0.07 m. Evidence: iteration 2 (y=0.07 with a lighter body) scored 47.8, the lowest of the five iterations, and iteration 1 (wheel_track 0.12 m) scored 55.1, below both narrower-track iterations.
